## Example 3.10 · The two middle observations {#l2-example-3-10 .compact}

Consider the dataset **1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 3**.

a) Find the median and mode directly from the ordered list.
b) Complete the table.

| Value, $x$ | Frequency, $f$ | Cumulative frequency, $cf$ |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1 | 1 | |
| 2 | 3 | |
| 3 | 4 | |

c) Explain how the table identifies the fourth and fifth observations.
d) Draw a frequency histogram and a cumulative frequency polygon, and identify the mode and median on the appropriate graphs.
<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 46 · Example 3.10 · Complete the working in your booklet.</p>

::: notes
cf1,4,8. Median(2+3)/2=2.5; mode3. cf4 atx2 means the4th observation is2; the5th is3. Unit-width cumulative polygon points(.5,0),(1.5,1),(2.5,4),(3.5,8). Here the graph at cf4 coincides with2.5; this coincidence does not replace locating both middle observations.
:::
